name: Teojomulco Chatino
world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

sources.citation: Campbell, Eric W. 2013. The internal diversification and subgrouping of Chatino. IJAL 79(3): 395-420.
sources.note: Family-level only: 'prominent vowels are those in root-final syllables' (p. 401); fn. 10 (p. 402) Zapotec root-initial prominence is 'the opposite of Chatino'. Teojomulco is not among the varieties treated ('TEO' there = Teotepec).

No descriptive references listed. Comment: 'Chatino from Teojomulco was documented by a wordlist in Belmar, Francisco 1902 before it went extinct. As shown by J. Ryan Sullivant 2016 this turns out to be the most divergent of the Chatino languages'.

Second-hand: Belmar 1902 wordlist of 228 words/phrases is the only data; reconstructed 5 vowels, 15 consonants; '/t͡s/ is a post-tonic allophone of /s/' -- implies Sullivant 2016 posits a tonic syllable, but the article does not say where it falls.

sources.citation: Sullivant, John Ryan. 2015. The Phonology and Inflectional Morphology of Cháʔknyá, Tataltepec de Valdés Chatino, a Zapotecan Language. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Austin.
sources.access_detail: copy on file; access check: not located online or at Harvard
sources.note: Phonology chapter is about Tataltepec Chatino only. Teojomulco appears pp. 9, 13, 32-33 as a classification note: Belmar (1902) transcribed it, 'a Chatino language even more divergent than Zenzontepec Chatino'; Belmar's transcription 'somewhat inexpertly transcribed, failing to regularly indicate vowel nasalization, stop prenasalization, glottal stops, and all tonal phenomena'. No stress statement for Teojomulco.

sources.citation: Campbell, Eric W. 2014. Aspects of the Phonology and Morphology of Zenzontepec Chatino, a Zapotecan Language of Oaxaca, Mexico. PhD dissertation, University of Texas at Austin.
sources.note: p. 18 only: Belmar (1902) includes parallel vocabulary lists from five communities incl. 'Teojomulco, which appears to be an otherwise unattested variety of Chatino even more divergent than Zenzontepec Chatino'. Nothing on Teojomulco prosody.

sources.citation: Belmar, Francisco. 1921. Glotología indígena mexicana. México. (archive.org glotologiaindgen00belm, scanned text)
